question: Should the durable approval contract intentionally terminally deny malformed, kind-mismatched, or disallowed verdicts while preserving requester and reviewer-device binding and cancelling prior-runtime pending records on Gateway restart?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and fail-closed, but these choices define security-sensitive public protocol and upgrade semantics that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept the fail-closed contract
options.body: Approve the current binding, malformed-verdict denial, restart cancellation, and retained terminal-record semantics as the durable Gateway contract.

options.title: Revise terminal error semantics
options.body: Require malformed requests to return non-terminal validation errors and update the schema, handlers, clients, and race proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the first increment
options.body: Split disputed authorization or restart policy from the durable store and defer the public unified RPC contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the fail-closed contract
recommendation.body: Approve the current binding, malformed-verdict denial, restart cancellation, and retained terminal-record semantics as the durable Gateway contract.
